summary: mymatasan's authorization catalog (`apps/mymatasan/services/rbac.go`'s `Policy()`) had no rule for `GET /api/auth/session`, the first call the SPA makes after a password is accepted to learn the signed-in user's role and must-change-password flag. Because the permission matrix is deny-by-default, that meant the `viewer` and `operator` roles could not complete sign-in at all: the password was accepted and the very next call returned "you do not have permission for this action". Only `admin`/`superadmin` ever worked, because a superadmin role bypasses the matrix entirely and so never exercised this path -- the three-role model was, in practice, a one-role model. Fixed by adding `{Path: "/api/auth/session", Viewer: read, Operator: read}` to the catalog. A second, deeper bug meant that fix alone would not have reached any install whose roles had already been seeded: `domain/shared/services/appliance_rbac.go`'s `EnsureApplianceRoles` skipped a role wholesale the moment it had any permission rows at all, so a rule added to the catalog after first boot was invisible to every existing install and only ever reached brand-new ones. `EnsureApplianceRoles` now backfills instead: a role with zero rows is still seeded in full, but a role that already has rows gets a row added only for a catalog path it has no row for at all, and an existing row's verbs are never touched -- so a site's hand-tuned permissions survive every reboot while a catalog addition still reaches them. Regression-tested at both layers (`apps/mymatasan/services/rbac_test.go`'s `TestPolicy_NonAdminRolesCanCompleteSignIn` walks the App.js sign-in sequence for viewer and operator; the new `domain/shared/services/appliance_rbac_test.go` covers empty-role seeding, never-touch-a-tuned-row, the backfill itself, and idempotency) and live-verified on a throwaway SQLite install, including simulating a pre-fix install by deleting the two session rows and confirming sign-in broke, then watching the backfill restore them on restart.
compatibility: Backward compatible. New installs get the corrected catalog on first boot as before. Existing installs get the missing `/api/auth/session` rows backfilled automatically on the next boot after upgrade -- no config change, no manual step, no re-seeding. No permission a site has already granted or denied by hand is touched by the backfill; only rows for catalog paths the role has none for at all are added. The evidentiary boundary is unaffected: viewer/operator still cannot reach recordings/observations/settings/users/roles beyond what the catalog already granted them.
